text.p: Heryanto Arbi lost his world badminton crown on Saturday, first tamed and then overwhelmed by Dane Peter Rasmussen.
The Indonesian raced to a 10-0 lead in the first game but Rasmussen survived the storm to triumph 9-15 15-9 15-2.
In Sunday's final Rasmussen will meet compatriot Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen or China's Sun Jun who were playing their semifinal later on Saturday.
It was Rasmussmen's biggest win to date but it hardly looked possible early on as Arbi racked up the points against a nervy-looking opponent.
Rasmussen hung on and when Arbi was called twice in the second set for service infringements it seemed to unsettle the Indonesian.
Growing in strength and confidence, Rasmussen powered his way to the final with a mixture of heavy left-handed smashing and some astute tactics.
The Dane, seeded 15, said: "I did not expect to win. I have met him twice and lost both matches. I was nervous about his attacking game which is very good."
Arbi, seeded only 12 here after a succession of injuries from mid-1995 saw him slip down the world rankings, looked a tired man at the end.

The defeat compounded a disappointing two weeks for Indonesia. Their top singles women, Susi Susanti and Mia Audina, lost in Friday's quarter-finals and last week the country had to yield to big rivals China in the Sudirman Cup team event.
Their hopes of a title now lie in the men's and women's doubles, although they face stiff opposition there as well.

Rasmussen's victory provided some compensation for Denmark whose mixed doubles pairing of Jens Eriksen and Marlen Thomsen failed gallantly in the final against the powerful Chinese pair of Liu Yong and Ge Fei, who won 15-5 16-17 15-4.
The Danes staved off five match points in the second game then captured it only to yield in the decider.
The Chinese had more to celebrate when women's singles titleholder Ye Zhaoying reached the final after beating compatriot Wang Chen 11-5 5-11 11-4.
